You are working in the container at /luxon, a checkout of the Luxon date library (JS, jest tests, babel, node v10). Do NOT use the internet. Do NOT modify any test files. Only edit /luxon/src/datetime.js (nothing else). Use /tmp for scratch files and delete them afterwards.

CONTEXT: `DateTime#isInDST` in /luxon/src/datetime.js (around line 1164) is:

  get isInDST() {
    if (this.isOffsetFixed) {
      return false;
    } else {
      return (
        this.offset > this.set({ month: 1 }).offset || this.offset > this.set({ month: 5 }).offset
      );
    }
  }

The bug: it decides "am I in DST" by comparing the current offset with the offset on the same day-of-month in January and in May of the same year. In years where DST starts in January (e.g. the USA in 1974, when DST ran from January 6 to October 27), the January comparison is against a date that is itself in DST, so isInDST wrongly returns false for the whole year. It must compare against a day that is reliably in standard time, i.e. January 1st.

TASK:
1) BASELINE: run `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -40` and record the exact list of failing tests (file + name) and totals.
2) BEFORE the edit, write a scratch script that prints isInDST for a set of dates (see the list in step 4) and run it, so the before/after difference is visible. Run scratch scripts with `cd /luxon && npx babel-node /tmp/check3.js` if that works; if babel-node does not pick up the repo's .babelrc for files in /tmp, instead create the scratch test file INSIDE /luxon but NOT under test/ (e.g. /luxon/tmpcheck.test.js) so jest picks up the babel config, run it with `cd /luxon && npx jest tmpcheck.test.js 2>&1 | tail -60`, and DELETE it afterwards. Never modify or delete existing test files.
3) Apply exactly this change: replace `this.set({ month: 1 }).offset` with `this.set({ month: 1, day: 1 }).offset` in the isInDST getter. Change nothing else in the file (keep prettier formatting; `npx prettier --check src/datetime.js` should be clean, or run `npx prettier src/datetime.js > /tmp/p.js && diff /tmp/p.js src/datetime.js` to confirm no formatting drift, then delete /tmp/p.js).
4) VERIFY with the scratch script, printing for each case the value of isInDST:
   - For every day of 1974 in zone "America/New_York": the set of days where isInDST is true must be exactly Jan 6 .. Oct 27 inclusive (report the first and last true day, and the count of true days).
   - DateTime.fromISO("1974-01-05", { zone: "America/New_York" }).isInDST -> false
   - DateTime.fromISO("1974-01-06", { zone: "America/New_York" }).isInDST -> true
   - DateTime.fromISO("1974-07-01", { zone: "America/New_York" }).isInDST -> true
   - DateTime.fromISO("1974-10-27", { zone: "America/New_York" }).isInDST -> true
   - DateTime.fromISO("1974-10-28", { zone: "America/New_York" }).isInDST -> false
   - DateTime.fromISO("1982-05-25", { zone: "America/Los_Angeles" }).isInDST -> true
   - DateTime.fromISO("1982-01-25", { zone: "America/Los_Angeles" }).isInDST -> false
   - DateTime.fromISO("1982-12-25", { zone: "America/Los_Angeles" }).isInDST -> false
   - DateTime.fromISO("2016-01-15", { zone: "Australia/Sydney" }).isInDST -> true (southern hemisphere: January is DST)
   - DateTime.fromISO("2016-07-15", { zone: "Australia/Sydney" }).isInDST -> false
   - DateTime.fromISO("2016-06-15", { zone: "UTC" }).isInDST -> false
   - DateTime.invalid("because").isInDST -> falsy
   Report the actual values.
5) Re-run the full suite `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -40` and confirm the set of failures is identical to the baseline (no previously-passing test may fail).
6) Report `cd /luxon && git status --porcelain` and `git diff src/datetime.js`.

Report concisely: baseline failures, before/after script output, post-fix test results, git status/diff. Note: another agent may be concurrently editing src/interval.js and src/impl/util.js; that is expected and not your concern. Do not touch those files.

You are working in the container at /luxon, a checkout of the Luxon date library (JS, jest tests, babel, node v10). Do NOT use the internet. Do NOT modify any test files. Only edit /luxon/src/duration.js (nothing else). Use /tmp for scratch files and delete them afterwards.

CONTEXT: In /luxon/src/duration.js, the conversion matrices `lowOrderMatrix`, `casualMatrix` and `accurateMatrix` list, for each unit, how many of each smaller unit it contains (e.g. `quarters: { months: 3, weeks: 13, days: 91, ... }`). The `casualMatrix`'s `quarters` row is missing the `seconds` entry, while `years` and `months` have theirs and the `accurateMatrix`'s `quarters` row has `seconds: (daysInYearAccurate * 24 * 60 * 60) / 4`. Because of that, converting between quarters and seconds yields NaN, e.g. `Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1, seconds: 5 }).normalize()` produces `quarters: NaN` and `Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1 }).shiftTo("seconds")` produces NaN. The value must be consistent with `days: 91`, i.e. 91 * 24 * 60 * 60 = 7862400 seconds per quarter.

TASK:
1) BASELINE: run `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -40` and record the exact list of failing tests (file + name) and totals.
2) BEFORE the edit, write a scratch script that prints the cases in step 4 and run it, so the before/after difference is visible. Run scratch scripts with `cd /luxon && npx babel-node --only '/tmp' /tmp/check4.js` (plain `npx babel-node /tmp/check4.js` may fail on syntax because files outside cwd are not transformed; if it fails, instead put a scratch test file INSIDE /luxon but NOT under test/ (e.g. /luxon/tmpcheck.test.js), run `cd /luxon && npx jest tmpcheck.test.js 2>&1 | tail -60`, and DELETE it afterwards). Never modify or delete existing test files.
3) Apply exactly this change: in `casualMatrix`, in the `quarters` object, insert `seconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60,` between the `minutes: 91 * 24 * 60,` line and the `milliseconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` line. Change nothing else in the file (keep prettier formatting; verify with `npx prettier src/duration.js > /tmp/p.js && diff /tmp/p.js src/duration.js`, then delete /tmp/p.js).
4) VERIFY with the scratch script, printing results for:
   - Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1, seconds: 5 }).normalize().toObject()  -> must have no NaN (expected { quarters: 1, seconds: 5 })
   - Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1 }).shiftTo("seconds").toObject()      -> expected { seconds: 7862400 }
   - Duration.fromObject({ seconds: 7862400 }).shiftTo("quarters").toObject() -> expected { quarters: 1 }
   - Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1 }).shiftTo("minutes").toObject()      -> expected { minutes: 131040 }
   - Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1, seconds: 7862400 }).normalize().toObject() -> expected { quarters: 2 }
   - Duration.fromObject({ years: 1, quarters: 1 }).normalize().toObject()    -> expected { years: 1, quarters: 1 }
   - A loop over ALL ordered pairs (u1, u2) of the units ["years","quarters","months","weeks","days","hours","minutes","seconds","milliseconds"]: for each pair build `Duration.fromObject({ [u1]: 1, [u2]: 1 }).normalize()` and check that every value in toObject() is a finite number (not NaN), and also check `Duration.fromObject({ [u1]: 1 }).shiftTo(u2)` yields a finite number. Report the list of any pairs that fail BEFORE the fix and confirm that NONE fail AFTER the fix. Also do the same loop with `conversionAccuracy: "longterm"`.
   - Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1, seconds: 5 }).normalize().toISO() -> report the string.
5) Re-run the full suite `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -40` and confirm the set of failures is identical to the baseline (no previously-passing test may fail).
6) Report `cd /luxon && git status --porcelain` and `git diff src/duration.js`.

Report concisely: baseline failures, before/after script output (especially the failing unit pairs before the fix), post-fix test results, git status/diff. Note: other agents may be concurrently editing src/interval.js, src/impl/util.js and s
